title: The Thlen Serpent and the Orphan (U Thlen Bad Ka Wanduh)
cultural_context: The epic confrontation between the evil man-eating dragon/serpent U Thlen of Dainthlen and the heroic youth who slayed it to liberate the Khasi people.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha Dainthlen ha krem ba dum,
U thlen u rieh ban nguid ia u briew,
U kpa u kpa u la leit noh,
Ka pyrthei baroh ka la rieh;
Hynrei u wanduh ba shlur
U la shim la ka tari ba nep,
Ban pynduh ia u ksuid basniew
Ba wan pynjot ia ka ri.

Da ka nar ba syaid ba la thang,
U la pynnguid ia u thlen ba khraw,
Ka mawsiang ka la pait,
Ka kshaid ka la pashat um;
La kut ka jingsheptieng u briew,
La laitluid u Hynniewtrep,
Ka nam jong u khlur ba shlur
Kan im ha man ka jingshai.
lyrics_english:
At Dainthlen within the dark cavern,
The Thlen serpent lurked to devour mankind,
Generation upon generation had perished,
The entire populace cowered in fear;
Yet the brave impoverished orphan
Took up his sharp-tempered iron blade,
To vanquish the demonic monster
That brought devastation upon the land.

With red-hot irons glowing from fire,
He fed the ravenous monster,
The giant rocks split asunder,
The waterfall surged with foam;
Mankind's mortal terror was broken,
The Seven Huts walked free again,
The name of that courageous warrior
Shall live in every morning light.
